II. General Title (of the Treatise-Writer) VIII. Origins of the Composition of the Treatise (2) 1. Introduction of the Chapter The general title of the treatise is as follows: *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya*, "Exegesis of the Treasury of Abhidharma. This title is established based on two factors: first, it indicates that this work is a commentary (*bhāṣya*) upon the *Abhidharmakośa-kārikā* composed by the Venerable Vasubandhu; second, it reveals that the subject matter contained herein is the *Abhidharma*. Regarding the origins of the composition of this treatise, there are two points of inquiry. First, one might ask: what was the purpose for which this treatise was composed? Second, one might ask: who is the author of this treatise? First, concerning the purpose for which this treatise was composed: the Venerable Vasubandhu, having previously composed the *Abhidharmakośa-kārikā*—which summarizes the essential doctrines of the Vaibhāṣika school of the Sarvāstivāda—composed this exegesis (*bhāṣya*) for the sake of providing a detailed explanation of those verses. Furthermore, he composed it so that those who desire to understand the profound meaning of the Abhidharma may easily comprehend it, and so that those who wish to refute the tenets of other schools may do so effectively. Thus, the primary purpose of this treatise is to provide a comprehensive exposition of the Abhidharma teachings. Second, concerning the author of this treatise: the author is the Venerable Vasubandhu. He was born into a Brahmin family in Puruṣapura (Peshawar) in northern India. From his youth, he was renowned for his mastery of the Vedas and various secular sciences. Later, he became a monk under the guidance of the Venerable Saṃghabhadra and studied the Abhidharma of the Sarvāstivāda school. Subsequently, he traveled to Ayodhyā, where he encountered the Venerable Manoratha, from whom he received the Mahāyāna teachings. Thereafter, he composed the *Vyākhyāyukti* and other works to clarify the Mahāyāna doctrine. It is said that he passed away at the age of eighty, after having extensively propagated the Dharma. Thus, the origins of the composition of this treatise are established through these two considerations: its purpose and its author. As for the specific circumstances of its composition, the Venerable Vasubandhu, residing in Ayodhyā, composed this exegesis while relying upon the *Abhidharmakośa-kārikā* as his basis, drawing from the vast scriptural authority of the Vaibhāṣikas and the insights of the Mahāyāna. This concludes the introduction to the chapter on the origins of the composition of the treatise.
